tos.title: Before you use Overture
tos.subtitle: This is Overture's own agreement — not the terms of whatever app you're about to deploy. Those come later, once you've picked one.
tos.point1: Your Cloudflare API Token stays in this browser tab only. Overture never sends it anywhere except Cloudflare's own API, and it is gone the moment you close the tab.
tos.point2: Overture writes no logs and keeps no record of what anyone deployed, when, or from where. There is nothing here for anyone — including whoever runs this Overture — to look up later.
tos.point3: Everything gets created in your own Cloudflare account, under your own billing. Overture itself owns nothing it deploys.
tos.point4: Every cost and every consequence of a deployment is yours to carry. Overture is a tool that acts on your instructions, not a party to what happens afterward.
tos.point5: A package from a source this Overture accepts can do anything its declared capabilities allow, inside your account. Read what it asks for before you agree to it.
tos.point6: Overture itself is free software, licensed under the AGPL, with its source open for anyone to read.
tos.point7: Overture is never sold. If anyone asks you to pay for "access" to a copy of it, that is a scam — walk away.

credentials.title: Cloudflare credentials
credentials.subtitle: The permissions below are the ones this package asks for. Only the required rows block the deployment.
credentials.createAccount: Create or sign in to Cloudflare
credentials.setupToken: Create a Custom Token in the target account's Account API Tokens.
credentials.accountIdHelp: Found on the right sidebar of any Cloudflare dashboard page.
credentials.apiTokenHelp: Use an account-level API Token (cfat_), not a Profile API Token.
credentials.apiTokenStorageNote: The token stays in this browser tab's session storage and is never sent anywhere but Cloudflare's own API. If the package asks to keep a copy as one of its own Workers Secrets, the confirmation page says so before you agree.
credentials.r2KeyHelp: An R2 S3 key pair, asked for because this package uses one for direct bucket access.
credentials.r2KeysPairRequired: Provide both R2 key fields, or leave both empty.
credentials.checksHelp: Read-only probes of your account, run before anything is created.
credentials.blocked: Something the package requires isn't satisfied yet. Fix the rows marked above, then re-check.

target.title: Worker and storage
target.subtitle: Names for what this deployment creates in your account, and the questions this package asks. Defaults come from the package.
target.scanning: Reading the Workers and storage in this account…
target.workerNameHelp: The Cloudflare Worker this app runs as. Storage names follow it until you edit them.
target.workerUnknown: Couldn't tell whether a Worker of this name already exists.
target.workerExists: A Worker named “{name}” already exists — this becomes an upgrade of that Worker.
target.workerFresh: No Worker named “{name}” exists yet; it will be created.
target.nameInvalid: Cloudflare names are 1–63 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.
target.overwriteConfirm: I confirm the existing Worker “{name}” is the installation I mean to update.
target.fullRebuild: Full rebuild — delete the Worker and recreate it from scratch
target.fullRebuildHelp: Stored data is kept: the databases, buckets and namespaces named below are reused as they are. The Worker script, its bindings, secrets, scheduled tasks and static assets are recreated, and custom domains have to reattach.
target.nameSkipped: Left empty — this resource is optional and will be skipped.
target.nameUnknown: Couldn't tell whether “{name}” already exists in this account.
target.nameExists: “{name}” already exists in this account and will be reused as it is. Make sure it isn't unrelated data.
target.nameAbsent: “{name}” doesn't exist in this account yet; it will be created.
target.containersHelp: This package can run part of itself in a container. Declaring one Cloudflare doesn't have, or dropping one it already runs, both cause trouble — so the default follows what the live Worker declares today.
target.domainInvalid: That isn't a hostname this package accepts.
target.patternAdvisory: This value doesn't match the format the package suggests. You can continue anyway.

confirm.title: Confirm before deploying
confirm.subtitle: Nothing has been created yet.
confirm.capabilitiesTitle: What this package is allowed to do
confirm.capabilitiesIntro: {app}'s deploy script runs sandboxed and can reach exactly the following, on your account, and nothing else.
confirm.capabilitiesNone: Nothing — this package's script has no account access at all.

capabilities.d1: Create D1 databases named above, and run SQL on them
capabilities.r2: Create the R2 buckets named above
capabilities.kv: Create the KV namespaces named above
capabilities.secrets: Set Workers Secrets on the Worker it deploys
capabilities.worker: Upload Worker versions and switch traffic to them, and delete the Worker on a full rebuild
capabilities.cron: Read and set the Worker's scheduled tasks
capabilities.domains: List custom domains and attach one to the Worker
capabilities.probe: Send a plain request to the deployed URL to see whether it answers

confirm.hostSecretsWarnTitle: This app will hold your Cloudflare credentials
confirm.hostSecretsWarnBody: The values below are written into the deployed Worker's own Secrets, so the app can call the Cloudflare API as you afterwards. The deploy script never reads them, but the running app can use them for anything the credential allows. Continue only if you trust this app with that.

deploy.title: Deploying
deploy.subtitle: Don't close this tab until this finishes.
deploy.configMissing: The install configuration is no longer loaded — go back and pick a release again.
deploy.retryFromHere: Retrying restarts the whole deployment. Anything already created is reused.

hostSteps.download: Fetch and verify the deploy package

done.title: {app} is live
done.propagationNotice: Cloudflare can take a couple of minutes to apply the changes and switch traffic over, so the first request may not answer right away.
done.saveWarning: These values are shown once and stored nowhere. Save them now.

policy.title: Deployment policy
policy.subtitle: Which repositories this Overture will accept a deploy package from.
policy.riskBody: With the allowlist off, this Overture will fetch and run a deploy package from any GitHub repository a visitor names — that package can still only do what its declared capabilities allow, but inside the visitor's own Cloudflare account.
policy.readOnlyHint: This page only displays the policy in effect. To change it, edit ALLOWLIST_ENABLED / ALLOWED_SOURCES in this deployment's wrangler.toml and redeploy the Worker.
